Oldenborn. Normalized Bad Eden ancestry root.

Select one heritage separately when building the character: Earthbound, Lumenwrought, Stormborn Nomad, Rustland Scavenger.

This root grants the shared Oldenborn core trait package and preserves live UUID compatibility for existing feature items.

“You are not an elf. You are the memory of a place that learned to walk again.”

Dream-Flesh. You do not sleep. When you rest, you drift into Yesod—symbolic memory-space—unless you choose otherwise. You are immune to magical sleep, and you can always tell when a dream, illusion, or constructed reality is present.

Old Memory, Old Paths. You reroll the lowest die on checks to interpret ruins, follow ley-lines, identify altered terrain, and sense metaphysical instability. You always know if a place feels remembered, abandoned, or contested (the GM answers vaguely).

Veil-Sight. You perceive the presence of spirits, ghosts, Spark echoes, and noospheric constructs. This grants awareness, not perfect sight.

You Are Remembered. When you first meet a community, the GM chooses (or rolls) whether you are met with reverence, fear, or familiarity. It’s never neutral.

“You were not beautiful. You were wanted.”

Glamourfield (At Will, Minor). You can create subtle illusions affecting light, sound, scent, or emotional tone. It never overwhelms; it always influences.

Dream Anchor. You have a +1 bonus to checks against metaphysical hazards (slippage, dream traps, Spark backlash).

⚔ AURABLADE — MECHANICAL CORE (PHASE 1.5)

Emotion is not flavor text.
Emotion is a resource.

🔥 Burn — What It Is (Plainly)

Burn represents emotional overextension:

  • Adrenaline overload

  • Suppressed fear

  • Moral fixation

  • Spiritual strain

Burn is not a die pool.
Burn is a state track that unlocks power and risk.

You do not “spend” Burn.
You enter Burn states, and the game responds.

🔥 How You Gain Burn (Concrete Triggers)

You gain 1 Burn when any one of the following occurs:

Universal Burn Triggers

  • You hit with an attack granted or enhanced by your Aura

  • You force a defense check using an Aura feature

  • You escalate without pause (GM-flagged high-risk continuation)

  • You remain in the same Aura for too long without stabilizing

⚠️ Limit:
You can gain at most 1 Burn per round, unless a subclass explicitly overrides this.

Burn rewards commitment, not spam.

🔥 Burn States (Explicit Bands)

Burn is divided into three states.

🔹 Burn 0–1 — Controlled

You are emotionally steady.

  • You gain only passive Aura benefits

  • No backlash risk

  • No forced effects

This is the safe state.

🔸 Burn 2–3 — Engaged

Your emotion is active and visible.

At this state:

  • Your Aura unlocks standard combat riders

  • Your abilities gain explicit 5E effects

  • You may choose to push harder

This is the intended combat state.

🔥 Burn 4+ — Overheated

You are exceeding safe emotional limits.

At this state:

  • Aura effects intensify

  • GM is authorized to:

    • Trigger backlash

    • Apply collateral

    • Force Aura collapse on a bad roll or narrative beat

This is the danger state.

🔥 What Happens at Backlash (Clear, Bounded)

When backlash triggers (GM discretion or subclass feature):

One of the following occurs (GM chooses or rolls):

  • You take psychic or sephirotic damage (radiant)

  • You suffer roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on your next attack or save

  • Your Aura collapses (you drop to Burn 0)

  • A narrative consequence occurs (fear, escalation, attention)

Aurablades are not punished randomly.
They are punished predictably.

💠 AURA STATES — EXPLICIT MECHANICAL EFFECTS

Each Aura grants:

  • A passive effect

  • Engaged Burn effects

  • Overheated Burn effects

These are not manifestations.
They are combat permissions.

🔥 FURY — Escalation & Force

Theme: Press harder. Break lines.

Passive (Always On)

  • +1 bonus to damage rolls with melee weapon attacks

Burn 2–3 (Engaged)

When you hit with a melee attack:

  • Deal +tier damage

  • You may push the target 1 square or cleave a second creature within reach (once per turn)

You may also:

  • Ignore roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on one attack per turn

Burn 4+ (Overheated)

When you hit:

  • Target must succeed on a Violence check or be knocked prone

  • Your attacks deny reactions until the start of your next turn

⚠️ Risk:

  • On a missed attack, GM may trigger backlash

Fury trades control for dominance.

🛡 RESOLVE — Defense & Refusal

Theme: Stand firm. Make removal expensive.

Passive (Always On)

  • +1 bonus to Guard while you have not moved this turn

Burn 2–3 (Engaged)

You may:

  • Gain resistance to one damage type until the start of your next turn

  • Ignore forced movement up to 2 squares

Additionally:

  • Opportunity attacks against you are made at disadvantage

Burn 4+ (Overheated)

You may:

  • Automatically succeed on one Violence, Body, or Intrigue check per round

  • Lock your position: enemies cannot move you at all

⚠️ Risk:

  • When damage is fully negated, backlash may occur

Resolve dares the world to try harder.

🤍 MERCY — Protection & Restraint

Theme: Prevent loss. Redirect harm.

Passive (Always On)

  • You may choose to deal nonlethal damage without penalty

Burn 2–3 (Engaged)

Once per round, when an ally within 2 squares takes damage:

  • Reduce that damage by tier

  • You may redirect it to yourself

You may also:

  • Automatically stabilize a creature you touch

Burn 4+ (Overheated)

You may:

  • Prevent an ally from dropping below 1 Integrity (once per round)

  • Convert a failed last stand check into a success

⚠️ Risk:

  • Preventing death may trigger backlash or Aura collapse

Mercy delays consequences — it does not erase them.

🕳 DREAD — Suppression & Collapse

Theme: Remove hope. End momentum.

Passive (Always On)

  • Enemies within 1 square suffer roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on morale-based checks (GM adjudication)

Burn 2–3 (Engaged)

On hit:

  • Target must save or be Shaken until the end of its next turn

  • Target cannot take reactions

You may also:

  • Suppress one buff or inspiration effect (GM adjudication)

Burn 4+ (Overheated)

When you hit:

  • Target suffers roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on all saves until the start of your next turn

  • Nearby enemies must save or hesitate (lose movement or reactions)

⚠️ Risk:

  • Collateral fear or narrative fallout is likely

Dread does not kill bodies.
It kills belief.

🔄 Changing Aura (Explicit Rule)

You may change your Aura:

  • As a bonus action

  • Or as part of a rest or narrative reset

Changing Aura:

  • Does not clear Burn automatically

  • May reduce Burn by 1 if done defensively or narratively

Frequent swapping = control
Deep commitment = power

🧠 How Players Should Think About Aurablade

Ask yourself every turn:

  • “Do I escalate — or stabilize?”

  • “Can I afford another Burn?”

  • “What happens if this goes wrong?”

Aurablades are not forgiving.

They are honest.

Oldenborn Heritage. The branch that lit up from inside. Festival-spirit, glamour-spirit, the ancestor that taught the people to call something beautiful before they had a word for sacred.

“The world remembered old names. You answered—and you were lit by the answering.”

Lumenwrought. You are the place-soul that learned to wear a mask of light. Folks call you elf, sylph, faerie, depending on what scares them prettier than it scares them honestly. You are the first reason a candle is holy.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Fey).

  • Size. Medium.

  • Lineage Lean. Your lineage leans toward PRE (Presence)—expressed primarily through Tier powers.

  • Glamourcast. You can shed dim light in a 1 square radius at will, and snuff it out the same way. Your light is the colour of one specific moment in your past—the GM and you decide which.

Bands: 0–1 Controlled, 2–3 Engaged, 4+ Overheated.

Open the Aurablade action dialog. Available options depend on your current Aura and Burn band.

This item should present only currently legal options for Fury, Resolve, Mercy, or Dread.
Open the Change Aura dialog and switch between Fury, Resolve, Mercy, and Dread.

“Emotion sharpens faster than steel.”

Aura States (Fury, Resolve, Mercy, Dread) shape a luminous blade. Spending power builds Burn; at high Burn you gain potency and risk backlash.
Open the Stabilize Burn dialog and reduce, clear, or safely manage Burn according to class/subclass rules.

Entropy has a shape. I cut along it.

Mode: Edge-walker · Drift: Sideways

Void Edge Aurablades cut along the seams of decay. The doctrine suppresses what enemies rely on — buffs, advantage, morale — and propagates dread into the spaces between people. Played as the operative whose presence makes hope harder to organize.

Doctrine Features

  • Level 3 — Null Field. Your blade suppresses advantage. When you hit at Burn 1+, suppress one of the following until the end of the target's next turn: reroll-lowest on attacks, bonus damage, or morale/inspiration effects. At Burn 3+ the target also loses one reaction.
  • Level 6 — Silence of Will. You break focus. Targets you hit roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on Clarity hold checks and cannot benefit from rallying or command effects. At Burn 3+, failing a Clarity hold also causes Burn-like fatigue (GM narrative).
  • Level 10 — Dread Cut. Fear propagates. When you hit at Burn 2+, the target saves or is Shaken; nearby enemies save or suffer hesitation (lose movement or reactions). At Burn 4+ fear spreads automatically to one additional creature.
  • Level 14 — Emotional Erasure. Once per round when you hit, remove one beneficial emotional, morale, or inspiration effect from the target. Bypasses resistance tied to hope or courage. At Burn 4+ the effect cannot be reapplied for 1 round.
  • Level 18 — Final Quiet (Capstone). Once per Soma Break, create a 6 squares zone for 1 minute: morale cannot rise, inspiration fails, hope/unity/courage buffs do not apply, enemies roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on checks vs fear. Afterward your Burn drops to 0.

“You are called. You will answer.”

Archetype (Bad Eden): Judgment (Reckoner). You are final account, exposure, and the terrifying moment when evasion ends. You force consequences to arrive on time.

Archetype Effects

  • Faction Edge. Your archetype strengthens revelation, decisive resolution, and moral or violent finality. This Archetype is associated with +1 Violence and +1 Faith in faction calculus.
  • Tier Engine. See this Archetype’s Tier feats (Tier 1–4) for your full tactical and strategic toolkit.

description.value:
Crew Type (Bad Eden): Covert Ops Cell.

“If you saw it happen, it wasn’t us.”

Covert Ops cells make wars quiet. They prefer locks to speeches, shadows to banners, and results to credit. They don’t start fights—they rearrange the board so the fight never happens.

  • Tactical Identity: You gain a skill rank in Stealth and with the Tinkering aptitude.
  • Strategic Identity: Your faction starts with +1 Intrigue OPs.

Judgment - Necessary force. +1 Violence, +1 Logistics OPs

Geburah draws the line. It rewards discipline, enforcement, and decisive action against fortified problems, but always risks becoming cruelty if severity outruns wisdom.

Occult Association (Bad Eden): Shaman.

“You don’t fix the world. You listen to what it’s trying to become.”

Shamans do not impose order. They enter into relationship.

To a Shaman, the Great Work is not about forcing alignment onto a dead world. It is about hearing the pulse that is still there and deciding whether to protect it, guide it, or stand aside long enough for it to speak clearly. Every Hex is alive in some way. Every leyline has mood. Every storm is making a decision. Every spirit remembers who treated the land like a partner and who treated it like inventory.

Where Kabbalists map structure and Alchemists force conversion, Shamans work by attunement. They negotiate with terrain, weather, spirits, and flow-states that existed before factions learned to count OP.

How Shamans pursue the Great Work:

  • By listening to terrain, weather, and spirit pressure
  • By stabilizing living systems instead of extracting from them
  • By redirecting corruption rather than merely containing it
  • By treating Hexes as relationships, not assets

Resonance: Netzach / Living Flow — endurance, ecology, instinctive continuity, and the intelligence of systems nobody designed.

Tell-tales: mud where there should not be mud, animals that stop running, weather that feels briefly conversational.

Faction Effect (Passive):

  • +1 specialty edge on relevant terrain, travel, weather, or wilderness-facing OP rolls (GM adjudicates the exact OP lane)

Cost Principle: attunement creates obligation. The more the land speaks to you, the less you can pretend not to hear it. Expect spirit attention, place-based duty, and backlash when your faction acts against the needs of a living Hex.

Tier 1 (Level 1) — Judgment (Reckoner)

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Faith and Intimidation.
  • Strategic: Your faction's passive OP bias now follows the base Archetype file.

Covert Ops cells make wars quiet. They prefer locks to speeches, shadows to banners, and results to credit. They don’t start fights—they rearrange the board so the fight never happens.

You’re learning the shape of your shadow. Expect mistakes. Budget for them.

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Stealth and with the Tinkering aptitude.
  • Strategic: Your faction starts with +1 Intrigue OPs.

Tier 1 — Shaman

“It was talking before. You just couldn’t hear it yet.”

At Tier 1, you become perceptible to the world and the world becomes perceptible to you.

You can feel when a place is hungry, when a storm is about to turn mean, and when a Hex is carrying more pressure than its surface suggests. You are not commanding Lore yet. You are learning its tone.

Tactical (Character Scale)

  • Gain a skill rank in Lore and Athletics
  • You can perform a brief attunement to sense whether a nearby area is spiritually calm, distressed, corrupted, or unusually resonant

Strategic (Faction Scale)

  • Hex Attunement: upon entering a new Hex, you learn one of the following about it: dominant flow-state, unusual weather pressure, leyline disturbance, or corruption presence
  • Once per Strategic Turn, gain +1 to one relevant travel, terrain, or wilderness-facing OP roll

Cost: once the world starts speaking to you, silence gets rare. Expect distraction, omen pressure, or spirit agitation when your faction ignores what a place is telling you.

A pre-Fall sports memorabilia foam finger. Faded blue. Slightly chewed at the base. Through some combination of polymer chemistry, nostalgia, and the structural ambitions of post-apocalyptic salvage, it is now load-bearing. Use it like a buckler. Wave it for morale. Both, on a good day.

Structural Foam. Counts as a buckler — +1 Guard while equipped in the off-hand. Once per scene, when you would take damage from a non-magical projectile, the foam absorbs the hit completely. The finger is not visibly damaged. The finger is, however, a little slower to wave.

Faded black cotton, unreasonably soft from a thousand washes, sized XL regardless of who's wearing it. The graphic is a band logo and tour list, both indistinct. Cities and dates the world no longer keeps. Wearers consistently describe the same vague dream — a stadium, a lighter held aloft, a single sustained chord — and consistently fail to remember it past breakfast.

Tour Memory. +1 to Resolve. While worn, you do not gain Stress from being homesick, lost, or out of your element. The shirt has been to bigger venues than this one. The shirt is unimpressed.

item.signature: The band name is unreadable. Wearers report dreams they can't quite remember. Probably a cool tour.

An unreasonably long woolen scarf, two-tone gray, that occasionally shifts position on its own. Sometimes it tightens against the neck on a cold night. Sometimes it falls off your shoulder for no reason. Sometimes, very quietly, when you are alone in a room, it purrs. The previous owner left it to you. The previous owner was very specific that this was a kindness.

Companion-Texture. +1 to Resolve while worn. Once per scene, when you would gain a Stress, you may pet the scarf instead. The Stress is averted. The scarf purrs faintly for a few seconds. Allies notice. Allies do not comment.

item.signature: Long. Soft. Occasionally purrs. The previous owner swears it was a cat. You believe them.

members.name: Marisol Quint
members.notes: She still cuts your travel papers for free because the last set you forged for her kept a Sweet Release skimmer out of a Monodynamic cage.

members.name: Ottway Reece
members.notes: Passes messages between you and three cells that would never speak to each other directly, and charges you nothing but a standing invitation to Sunday dinner you always mean to accept.

members.name: Beryl Achen
members.notes: Took the shot meant for you outside the Glasswick relay and lost two fingers to the frost after; she never brings it up, but you always check her gloves.

members.name: Ren Achak
members.notes: Kept the rhythm steady the night Toblerone's spirit-walk ran long and nearly didn't come back, and still won't say what she saw in the gap between beats.

members.name: Ossy Farrow
members.notes: Carved the bone mask Toblerone wore to bargain with something in the kudzu-choked hollow, and now refuses to make another, claiming the last one came back wrong.

members.name: Dell Marrow
members.notes: Owes Toblerone a debt neither will name aloud — a hawk let loose, a warning given late, a life saved by inches.
